Names and checks the urban regions built by `01a_Prepare_BUA_Groups.Rmd`
(read from `urban_region_checkpoints/`) and clips the National Forest
Inventory (NFI) woodland data to them. Re-run `01a` first if the input
data or a parameter changes.

```{r setup}
source(here::here("scripts", "00_setup.R"))
```

# Prepare BUA data (filter to England, join population)

Needed here as well as in `01a` because naming looks up each constituent
BUA's name and area from `bua`.

```{r prepare_bua_data}
# Filter to England using the LSOA-to-Region lookup rather than the
# census population table. LSOAs cover the whole country without gaps,
# whereas the census table's BUA22 codes do not match for central London,
# so a semi_join against it would drop inner London from `bua`.
england_buas <- lsoa_lookup |>
  filter(startsWith(RGN22CD, "E12")) |>
  distinct(BUA22CD)

bua <- bua |>
  semi_join(england_buas, by = "BUA22CD")

# Add population counts and names. A left_join keeps any BUA missing from
# the census population table, with population = NA.
bua <- bua |>
  left_join(
    census |>
      select(
        BUA22CD = `BUA code`,
        population = Counts,
        size_classification = `BUA size classification`
      ),
    by = "BUA22CD"
  )
```

# Name urban regions

Reads `urban_region_checkpoints/07_urban_regions_final.rds` (saved by
`01a_Prepare_BUA_Groups.Rmd`) and adds a name column, using `bua` (from
the chunk above) to look up each constituent BUA's name and area.

Limitation: for polycentric conurbations with no dominant BUA (for
example Blackwater Valley), the largest constituent may not be the
recognisable name for the group. A manual override table (below) handles
known cases.

Each group's constituent BUAs are found by matching geometry directly
(`st_equals`) rather than by reconstructing `bua_row_id` with
`row_number()`, which is not stable across separate runs.
`bua_grouped_raw`'s geometry is an exact, untransformed copy of each
constituent's original shape (01a Step 3B, before any buffering), so it
matches `bua` regardless of row order.

```{r name_urban_regions}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

bua_grouped_raw <- readRDS(
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "03c_bua_grouped_raw.rds")
)

urban_regions_final <- readRDS(
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "07_urban_regions_final.rds")
)

bua_matched <- st_join(
  bua_grouped_raw,
  bua |> select(BUA22CD, BUA22NM),
  join = st_equals
) |>
  mutate(bua_area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry))) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

n_unmatched <- sum(is.na(bua_matched$BUA22NM))
if (n_unmatched > 0) {
  cat(
    "WARNING:", n_unmatched, "of", nrow(bua_matched), "constituent BUAs",
    "had no exact geometry match in `bua` — check that `bua` in this",
    "session matches what 01a used to build the checkpoints.\n\n"
  )
}

# Naming rule, applied identically to every region. If one constituent
# BUA holds at least half of the group's total constituent area, the
# region is named after that BUA alone. Otherwise no single BUA
# dominates, and the region is named after its two largest constituents
# ("X & Y"). Ties on BUA area are broken arbitrarily.
region_names <- bua_matched |>
  group_by(closing_group) |>
  arrange(desc(bua_area_m2), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    total_constituent_area_m2 = sum(bua_area_m2),
    largest_bua_area_m2 = dplyr::first(bua_area_m2),
    largest_bua_name = dplyr::first(BUA22NM),
    second_bua_name = if (dplyr::n() >= 2) dplyr::nth(BUA22NM, 2) else NA_character_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    dominance_ratio = largest_bua_area_m2 / total_constituent_area_m2,
    bua_name = if_else(
      dominance_ratio >= 0.5 | is.na(second_bua_name),
      largest_bua_name,
      paste(largest_bua_name, "&", second_bua_name)
    )
  ) |>
  select(closing_group, bua_name, largest_bua_area_m2, dominance_ratio)

urban_regions_named <- urban_regions_final |>
  left_join(region_names, by = "closing_group") |>
  relocate(bua_name, .after = urban_region_id)

cat("Regions with a name assigned:", sum(!is.na(urban_regions_named$bua_name)), "/", nrow(urban_regions_named), "\n")

# Some groups remain split into several disjoint pieces after Step 7
# (London, for example, has a main piece and a separate satellite).
# Dissolve each group back into one (possibly multipart) feature before
# filtering, so a small satellite merges into its parent city rather than
# being judged against the sliver threshold on its own.
n_rows_before_dissolve <- nrow(urban_regions_named)

urban_regions_named <- urban_regions_named |>
  group_by(closing_group, bua_name, bua_count) |>
  summarise(
    area_ha = sum(area_ha),
    geometry = st_union(geometry),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat(
  "Dissolved", n_rows_before_dissolve, "pieces into",
  nrow(urban_regions_named), "regions (one per closing_group)\n"
)

# Drop groups that are still negligible after dissolving. This is a
# group-level total, so it removes only trivial groups (slivers and
# near-empty artefacts), not small satellite parts of a larger city.
min_area_ha <- 1

n_before_area_filter <- nrow(urban_regions_named)

urban_regions_named <- urban_regions_named |>
  filter(area_ha >= min_area_ha)

cat(
  "Dropped", n_before_area_filter - nrow(urban_regions_named),
  "regions below", min_area_ha, "ha (kept", nrow(urban_regions_named), ")\n"
)

# Name overrides for collective names where even the
# two-largest-constituents rule reads badly. The table currently holds one
# case, Blackwater Valley, a ten-town group that the rule would name after
# its two largest towns. Read from region_name_overrides.csv (see
# 00_setup.R) and matched by each group's set of constituent BUAs rather
# than by closing_group id, which is not stable across re-runs. Rows are
# added by hand.
constituent_keys <- bua_matched |>
  group_by(closing_group) |>
  summarise(
    constituent_key = paste(sort(unique(BUA22NM)), collapse = ";"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

name_override_lookup <- read.csv(
  region_name_overrides_file,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  rename(constituent_key = constituent_buas, override_name = collective_name)

override_by_group <- constituent_keys |>
  left_join(name_override_lookup, by = "constituent_key") |>
  select(closing_group, override_name)

cat(
  "Regions matched to a name override:",
  sum(!is.na(override_by_group$override_name)), "\n"
)

urban_regions_named <- urban_regions_named |>
  left_join(override_by_group, by = "closing_group") |>
  mutate(bua_name = if_else(!is.na(override_name), override_name, bua_name)) |>
  select(-override_name)

# Recompute urban_region_id, since dissolving and filtering changed the
# row count and order.
urban_regions_named <- urban_regions_named |>
  arrange(desc(area_ha)) |>
  mutate(urban_region_id = row_number()) |>
  relocate(urban_region_id, bua_name, closing_group, bua_count, area_ha, geometry)

saveRDS(
  urban_regions_named,
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "07b_urban_regions_named.rds")
)

st_write(
  urban_regions_named,
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "urban_regions_named.gpkg"),
  layer = "urban_regions",
  delete_layer = TRUE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Sorted by area to check the largest regions and their names.
urban_regions_named |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  arrange(desc(area_ha)) |>
  select(urban_region_id, bua_name, bua_count, area_ha) |>
  head(20) |>
  print()
```

# Labelled map (identify regions by name instead of guessing)

Run after the naming chunk (`urban_regions_named` must exist). Labels
only the largest N regions, because labelling all of them would be
unreadable.

```{r labelled_map}
top_n_labels <- 40

label_regions <- urban_regions_named |>
  arrange(desc(area_ha)) |>
  slice_head(n = top_n_labels)

label_coords <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(label_regions)))

plot(
  st_geometry(urban_regions_named),
  col = "grey70",
  border = "black",
  main = paste(
    nrow(urban_regions_named),
    "derived urban regions (top",
    top_n_labels,
    "labelled)"
  )
)

text(
  label_coords[, 1],
  label_coords[, 2],
  labels = label_regions$bua_name,
  cex = 0.6,
  col = "red",
  font = 2
)
```

# QA checks

Sanity checks on `urban_regions_named`. Run after the naming chunk.

```{r qa_checks}
cat("=== BASIC SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Total regions:", nrow(urban_regions_named), "\n")
cat("Total area (ha):", round(sum(urban_regions_named$area_ha), 1), "\n")
cat("Regions with no name assigned:", sum(is.na(urban_regions_named$bua_name)), "\n")

cat("\n=== AREA DISTRIBUTION (ha) ===\n")
print(summary(urban_regions_named$area_ha))

# Slivers: small leftover fragments from the Step 7 split are expected in
# small numbers; a large count would suggest over-fragmentation.
cat("\n=== SLIVER REGIONS (<1 ha) ===\n")
cat("Count:", sum(urban_regions_named$area_ha < 1), "\n")
cat(
  "Combined area of all slivers (ha):",
  round(sum(urban_regions_named$area_ha[urban_regions_named$area_ha < 1]), 2),
  "\n"
)

# Groups that split into several regions. Pieces from the same original
# group share a name and bua_count, because those are properties of the
# group rather than of the fragment; keep this in mind when interpreting
# bua_count.
cat("\n=== GROUPS SPLIT INTO MULTIPLE REGIONS ===\n")
split_groups <- urban_regions_named |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(closing_group, name = "n_pieces") |>
  filter(n_pieces > 1)

cat("Number of original groups that split into >1 region:", nrow(split_groups), "\n")
cat("Largest split (most pieces from one group):", max(split_groups$n_pieces), "\n")

cat("\nThe 15 groups that split into the most pieces:\n")
urban_regions_named |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  semi_join(slice_max(split_groups, n_pieces, n = 15), by = "closing_group") |>
  group_by(closing_group, bua_name) |>
  summarise(
    n_pieces = n(),
    total_area_ha = sum(area_ha),
    largest_piece_ha = max(area_ha),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n_pieces)) |>
  print(n = 15)

# Naming check for groups with several pieces. bua_name belongs to the
# whole closing_group, so the largest piece always carries it. This
# instead flags groups whose bua_count is high relative to the named
# BUA's own area, meaning many small BUAs were merged under one possibly
# unrepresentative name.
cat("\n=== POSSIBLE POLYCENTRIC NAMING MISMATCHES ===\n")
cat("(high bua_count relative to region size can indicate a merged\n")
cat("conurbation named after a non-dominant constituent, like Blackwater Valley)\n\n")

urban_regions_named |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(closing_group, bua_name) |>
  summarise(total_area_ha = sum(area_ha), bua_count = first(bua_count), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(ha_per_bua = total_area_ha / bua_count) |>
  arrange(ha_per_bua) |>
  filter(bua_count >= 10) |>
  head(15) |>
  print()

cat("\n=== TOP 20 REGIONS BY AREA (post-fix) ===\n")
urban_regions_named |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  arrange(desc(area_ha)) |>
  select(urban_region_id, bua_name, closing_group, bua_count, area_ha) |>
  head(20) |>
  print()
```

# National map (publication quality)

Requires `ggrepel`.

Design choices: sequential viridis fill on a log scale, because region
area is strongly right-skewed and a linear scale would show no variation
among smaller cities; viridis is perceptually uniform and colourblind
safe. Polygon borders are omitted because with over 3,000 regions they
read as noise at national scale. The 20 largest regions are labelled
using ggrepel, so labels do not overlap.

```{r national_map}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(scales)

top_n_labels <- 20

label_regions <- urban_regions_named |>
  arrange(desc(area_ha)) |>
  slice_head(n = top_n_labels)

label_coords <- st_centroid(st_geometry(label_regions)) |>
  st_coordinates() |>
  as.data.frame()

label_regions <- bind_cols(
  st_drop_geometry(label_regions),
  label_coords
)

national_map <- ggplot(urban_regions_named) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = area_ha), colour = NA) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = label_regions,
    aes(X, Y, label = bua_name),
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour = "grey15",
    bg.color = "white",
    bg.r = 0.15,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    seed = 1
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name = "Area (ha)",
    trans = "log10",
    labels = label_comma()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Derived urban regions of England",
    subtitle = paste0(
      nrow(urban_regions_named),
      " regions, from ONS Built-Up Areas 2022 (BUA22)"
    ),
    caption = "Boundaries derived via morphological closing of BUA22 polygons"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey40"),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey50", size = 8),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

national_map

ggsave(
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "national_map.png"),
  national_map,
  width = 10,
  height = 12,
  dpi = 300
)

cat("Saved to:", file.path(checkpoint_dir, "national_map.png"), "\n")
```

# Export AOI boundary for EDINA Digimap

Produces a single dissolved boundary covering all urban regions, for
uploading to EDINA Digimap's AOI tool so that the OS MasterMap Natural
Environment download is limited to where the urban regions are. The
boundary only sets a download extent and is not used in any analysis, so
it is lightly simplified to keep the upload file small.

```{r export_digimap_aoi}
library(sf)

aoi_dir <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "digimap_aoi")

dir.create(aoi_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

aoi_geom <- urban_regions_named |>
  st_geometry() |>
  st_union() |>
  st_simplify(dTolerance = 10, preserveTopology = TRUE)

aoi_boundary <- st_sf(
  name = "urban_regions_aoi",
  geometry = aoi_geom
)

st_write(
  aoi_boundary,
  file.path(aoi_dir, "urban_regions_aoi.shp"),
  delete_layer = TRUE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

cat("AOI boundary saved to:\n", file.path(aoi_dir, "urban_regions_aoi.shp"), "\n\n")
cat("CRS:", st_crs(aoi_boundary)$input, "\n")
cat("Combined area (ha):", round(as.numeric(st_area(aoi_boundary)) / 10000, 1), "\n\n")
cat("Files created:\n")
print(list.files(aoi_dir, full.names = FALSE))
```

# Clip NFI to all urban regions (national, not just the MK test)

Clips the national NFI file (4.36 GB) to the parts that intersect an
urban region, using the dissolved boundary from `export_digimap_aoi` as
the filter. Run that chunk first so that `aoi_boundary` exists. Woodland
is taken as the union of LCM and NFI (a cell counts if either source
classes it as woodland); this is implemented in
`02_Resistance_Surface.Rmd`, which consumes `nfi_urban`.

Two-stage filter:

1. Stage 1 reads the local file with `wkt_filter`. The GeoJSON is in
   WGS84 (CRS84), and GDAL compares filter coordinates with the layer's
   own CRS without reprojecting, so `aoi_boundary` is reprojected to
   WGS84 first. GeoJSON has no spatial index, so this is one sequential
   scan of the whole file.
2. Stage 2 applies a precise `st_intersects()` against the region
   shapes, after an explicit `st_transform()` (both objects are nominally
   EPSG:27700 but fail sf's strict CRS equality check). It is kept as a
   safeguard because GDAL's spatial filter may test only bounding boxes
   for this driver.

The result is checkpointed, so this only needs to run once.

```{r clip_nfi_urban_regions}
library(sf)

# aoi_boundary exists in memory only if export_digimap_aoi has run in
# this session; otherwise load it from the shapefile that chunk saves.
if (!exists("aoi_boundary")) {

  aoi_boundary_path <- file.path(
    checkpoint_dir, "digimap_aoi", "urban_regions_aoi.shp"
  )

  if (file.exists(aoi_boundary_path)) {
    cat("aoi_boundary not in memory — loading it from the saved\n")
    cat("shapefile (from a previous run of export_digimap_aoi).\n\n")
    aoi_boundary <- st_read(aoi_boundary_path, quiet = TRUE)
  } else {
    stop(
      "aoi_boundary not found in memory or on disk at ",
      aoi_boundary_path, ". Run the export_digimap_aoi chunk first ",
      "(it needs urban_regions_named, from name_urban_regions)."
    )
  }
}

cat("Stage 1: reading NFI within the urban-region boundary directly\n")
cat("from the local file, filtered in the file's own CRS (WGS84).\n")
cat("This is a full scan of the 4.36 GB file — expect a few minutes.\n\n")

aoi_boundary_wgs84 <- st_transform(aoi_boundary, 4326)
aoi_wkt <- st_as_text(st_geometry(aoi_boundary_wgs84))

t_nfi_bbox <- system.time({
  nfi_bbox_subset <- st_read(nfi_file, wkt_filter = aoi_wkt, quiet = TRUE)
})

print(t_nfi_bbox)
cat("\nNFI features within urban-region boundary:", nrow(nfi_bbox_subset), "\n\n")

# nfi_bbox_subset is read in WGS84 (the file's native CRS); transform it
# back to British National Grid to match aoi_boundary.
nfi_bbox_subset <- st_transform(nfi_bbox_subset, st_crs(aoi_boundary))

cat("Stage 2: precise intersection against the actual region shapes\n")
cat("(this is now working against a much smaller in-memory subset,\n")
cat("not the full 641,642 national features)...\n")

t_precise <- system.time({
  intersects_urban <- st_intersects(nfi_bbox_subset, aoi_boundary, sparse = FALSE)[, 1]
  nfi_urban <- nfi_bbox_subset[intersects_urban, ]
})

print(t_precise)

cat("\nNFI features intersecting urban regions:", nrow(nfi_urban), "\n")
cat("Combined NFI woodland area (ha):", round(sum(nfi_urban$Area_Ha), 1), "\n")

saveRDS(
  nfi_urban,
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "nfi_urban_regions.rds")
)

st_write(
  nfi_urban,
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "nfi_urban_regions.gpkg"),
  layer = "nfi_urban_regions",
  delete_layer = TRUE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

cat("\nSaved to:\n")
cat(" -", file.path(checkpoint_dir, "nfi_urban_regions.rds"), "\n")
cat(" -", file.path(checkpoint_dir, "nfi_urban_regions.gpkg"), "\n")
```

# National LCM vs NFI woodland map

Side-by-side view of LCM and NFI woodland coverage at national scale.
Needs `clip_nfi_urban_regions` to have finished. LCM is aggregated from
10 m to 200 m cells (`fact = 20`, modal resampling), because full
national detail is not visible at country scale and plotting England at
full resolution is slow. Increase `agg_factor` for a coarser, faster map.

```{r national_lcm_nfi_map}
library(terra)

agg_factor <- 20  # 10m x 20 = 200m cells

aoi_bbox_sf <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(aoi_boundary))

cat("Cropping national LCM to the urban-regions extent...\n")

t_lcm_crop <- system.time({
  lcm_national <- rast(lcm_file) |>
    crop(vect(aoi_bbox_sf))
})

print(t_lcm_crop)

cat("Aggregating from 10m to", agg_factor * 10, "m cells...\n")

t_lcm_agg <- system.time({
  lcm_national_agg <- aggregate(lcm_national[[1]], fact = agg_factor, fun = "modal")
})

print(t_lcm_agg)

lcm_woodland_national <- lcm_national_agg %in% c(1, 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))

plot(
  lcm_woodland_national,
  col = c("grey90", "darkgreen"),
  legend = FALSE,
  axes = FALSE,
  main = paste0("LCM woodland, England (", agg_factor * 10, "m cells)")
)

plot(
  st_geometry(nfi_urban),
  col = "darkgreen",
  border = NA,
  main = "National Forest Inventory (urban regions)"
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

The combined national woodland layer, and everything built on it (zoom
plots and per-region rankings), is in `02_Resistance_Surface.Rmd`.
